drug_drug_interactions.explanation: Concurrent administration of warfarin (vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant) and aspirin (antiplatelet) significantly increases the risk of severe gastrointestinal and major systemic hemorrhage due to additive antithrombotic pharmacodynamics.
drug_drug_interactions.source: FDA Prescribing Information for Warfarin Sodium; CHEST 9th Ed. Antithrombotic Therapy Guidelines

drug_drug_interactions.explanation: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen inhibit platelet COX-1 and cause gastric mucosal ulceration, markedly increasing bleeding complications when combined with systemic anticoagulants like warfarin.
drug_drug_interactions.source: FDA Drug Safety Communication: Prescription and OTC NSAIDs and Warfarin Bleeding Risks

drug_drug_interactions.explanation: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone secretion, causing renal potassium retention. Concomitant administration of potassium supplements increases the risk of clinically significant hyperkalemia.
drug_drug_interactions.source: AHA/ACC Heart Failure Guidelines; DailyMed Lisinopril Drug Interaction Section 7

drug_drug_interactions.explanation: Demonstration Test Rule: Fluoroquinolones may alter glycemic control, producing hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia in patients on oral biguanides. Monitor blood glucose closely.
drug_drug_interactions.source: Demo Fixture: OPD Hackathon Prototype Test Rule (Explicitly Marked Demo Only)
